verified_contract: The persisted contract implements queued, validating, awaiting_confirmation, uploading, processing, publishing, published, failed, cancelling, cancelled and unknown_remote states with an explicit legal transition table.
Every update uses an expected version compare-and-swap; the atomic file store fsyncs a temporary record, renames it and fsyncs the parent directory.
A SHA-256 identity binds tenant, platform, account, asset digest and immutable intent key; upload and publish derive stable stage keys from it.
Failure normalization distinguishes transient, permanent, auth, quota, policy and ambiguous unknown-remote outcomes.
Transient retries are bounded, jittered and Retry-After aware; ambiguous upload, publish or cancel outcomes are never blindly repeated.
Cancellation, manual retry, restart enumeration and explicit remote reconciliation are deterministic and append actor/timestamp transition history.
Injected response loss at upload and publish boundaries proves reconciliation can recover without duplicate remote calls.
boundary: This is a durable platform-neutral lifecycle and adapter contract. OCP-05 through OCP-08 must supply official platform adapters and their precise reconciliation semantics before any owner-gated live action.
